findings.claim: Every CheckPolicy/ruleDelta test edits the work branch without committing (newPolicyRepo checks out 'work' at the main tip and no test commits on it), so merge-base(HEAD, base) always equals HEAD and the committed-on-branch path of the policy gate is never exercised. Mutating ruleDelta to call GitChangedFiles(ctx, root, "HEAD") instead of base (or GitChangedFiles to diff against HEAD) keeps the whole suite green, while in production an agent branch that COMMITS a protected-scope rule addition (the normal state once ACTION-IMPL-EXEC-016 commits every turn) would drop out of the delta and pass a gated/strict repo unflagged.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/acdsl/policy_test.go:38-52 (newPolicyRepo commits only on main, then 'checkout -q -b work'), every TestCheckPolicy* and TestRuleDelta body (all use writePolicyFile without a policyGit commit on work), TestCheckPolicyNewUntrackedPolicyOnBranch:291-306 (commit only on main). Re-read internal/acdsl/git.go:46-66 (GitChangedFiles diffs against base, documented to cover committed changes) and policy.go:195-217/237-280 (base = merge-base). With no branch commit, base == HEAD, so base-vs-HEAD substitutions are indistinguishable to the suite. go test ./internal/acdsl/ green at head.
findings.fix: Add a TestCheckPolicy case (or TestRuleDelta case) that commits a protected-scope rule addition and a registry.json edit on the work branch (policyGit add/commit) before calling CheckPolicy, asserting both diagnostics.
